en.html:
Hikaru's body had returned to life.
Yesterday, in that one moment. In an instant.

The hair she had lost. Her teeth.
Flesh where almost only skin remained.
The withered-branch frame of her body.

Everything restored, fresh and full of life.

...Naturally.
Ordinary reason had no arrangement for such an event.

Something beyond ordinary reason had done it.
The power of a tsurugi, surely.

A true-forged tsurugi enormously increased its wielder's physical abilities. The power to recover was included.

An armoured warrior could lose an arm and, with it reattached, eventually recover. There were even stories of one growing back.

Put Hikaru's extraordinary recovery down to a tsurugi, and the explanation made sense.

One small difficulty.
It could not have happened.

A true-forged tsurugi could hasten healing even when not worn, even from far away. That much, yes. But only because it shared a mysterious bond with its wielder.

The warrior houses had an ancient rite: Tatewaki, the Sword-Bearing Ceremony. Warrior and tsurugi met, questioned each other's qualities, and accepted each other. One as wielder. One as weapon.

ja.html:
光の肉体は蘇生を遂げていた。
　昨日の、あの刹那――――<ruby>一瞬にして<rt>・・・・・</rt></ruby>。

　抜け落ちていた髪も、歯も、
　皮ばかりであった肉も、
　枯れ枝さながらの骨格も。

　全てが瑞々しく再生していた。

　……無論。
　そのような事が、常理の範疇で起こるわけがない。

　あれを成したのは、常理を超えるちから――
　劒冑の力であろう。

　真打の劒冑は<ruby>仕手<rt>シテ</rt></ruby>……使い手の身体能力を飛躍的に
向上させる。
　その中には回復力も含まれる。

　武者は腕を切り落とされても、<ruby>繋いでおけば<rt>・・・・・・</rt></ruby>やがて
元に戻る。
　<ruby>生え変わる<rt>・・・・・</rt></ruby>ことさえあるという。

　光の見せた異常回復も、劒冑の作用とみれば納得が
いく。
　
　だが有り得ない。

　真打劒冑は仕手に装甲されておらずとも、離れ離れ
になっていても、傷の回復を早める程度の真似はする。
　しかしそれは仕手と<ruby>奇<rt>く</rt></ruby>しき<ruby>縁<rt>えにし</rt></ruby>で結ばれていればこそ
の事だ。

　<ruby>帯刀の儀<rt>タテワキ</rt></ruby>と呼ばれる武家古伝の儀礼がある。
　これは武人と劒冑とが対面して互いの資質を問い、
使い手として武器として双方が承認し合う――という
ものである。

en.html:
Only after that rite did warrior and tsurugi become one. A new being, an armoured warrior with extraordinary powers. The two souls were inseparable; distance, however vast, could not divide them.

Hikaru could not have performed that rite.
With her mind shattered, how could a tsurugi recognise her as its master?

Indeed, she was still lying in bed.
Body restored. Any sign of getting up? None.

en.html:
From the tsurugi, also nothing. Afterward, confused or not, everyone had decided first to finish the ceremony. It had been carried through, the sacred doors closed, the tsurugi safely sealed again. Throughout, not one movement.

Hikaru and the silver tsurugi had formed a bond? I could not believe it.

And yet her extraordinary recovery allowed no explanation except the tsurugi's power.

Old tales, new tales, east or west—where was there a warrior's story like this? I had certainly never heard one.

Nothing made sense. Perhaps that was why I could not leap for joy, although surely I should have been doing exactly that.

My foster mother seemed much the same. Yesterday the Head and the other dignitaries had dispersed with anxious faces. No idea what had happened, but perhaps something very wrong.

...Really.
What had happened?

　余りにも不可解。
　だからだろう。本来なら躍り上がって喜んでも良い
筈なのに、とてもそんな気分になれないのは。

　養母も同じようなものらしい。

何か<ruby>良からぬこと<rt>・・・・・・</rt></ruby>が起きてしまったのかも――そんな
不安げな面持ちで、昨日は散会していった。

　……本当に。
　あれは、何だったのだろう。

en.html:
One final swing, as though I could sweep off whatever clung to me. Then I put the wooden sword away.

Hikaru's body had recovered. Good. That was good.

But a tsurugi had been involved. And which tsurugi? The 'evil thing' the Minato clan was commanded to keep sealed, past, present and future.

That part would not leave my mind. Without knowing why, I grew restless. My heart hurried along with it.

Good fortune?
Or calamity?

Still no answer. Like staring at the cup over the dice in an odd-or-even wager.

With gambling, the result at least must be shown. The numbers decide whether you win or lose.

If this was a wager...
what numbers were waiting underneath—

　だが、それに関与したのは劒冑。
　しかも、皆斗家が過去現在未来に渡って封ずるべし
と定められた〝邪しきもの〟だ。

　そこが心に引っ掛かってならない。
　わけもなく気が焦り、胸の動悸が慌しくなる。


　これは吉事か。
　それとも凶事か。

　未だ、判然としない。
　まるで丁半賭博の、<ruby>賽子<rt>さい</rt></ruby>を隠す壷を見ているような
心地だ。

　賭博であれば、結果は必ず示される。
　出目が勝ち負けを決める。

　これが賭博であるなら……
　果たして、どんな出目が――

Hikaru was there.

In the soft afternoon sunlight,
my sister stood there.

Until a year ago, such a familiar sight.◆
In this one year, so far away.◆
I had wanted to see it again so desperately, and still, little by little, the memory had blurred.

Hikaru was smiling.

—Hikaru was here.

　ただこの奇跡に感謝する。
　それが何であれ感謝する！

As if drawn toward her, my foster mother approached.
Her eyes were already wet.

en.html:
Not simply overcome by emotion. That was not how it looked.
My foster mother's face startled me.

She was bewildered.
Not doubting her eyes at an impossible miracle. Something else.

Her daughter had recovered. She accepted that.
And even so, something would not let her feel simple joy.

What?

...She was looking at Hikaru.
At Hikaru's face.

Hikaru was facing her mother too.
Showing her that expression.

en.html:
Impossible, I thought.
Look again. And again. The expression did not change.

Hikaru's smile was full of malice.
My foster mother took it without a sound.

Never before.

Before the illness, Hikaru had sometimes rebelled against her mother. Adolescence, probably. But this look? Not once.

...She had only just awakened. Perhaps there was some confusion.
Unless I told myself that, how was I to accept it?

馬鹿な、と。
　何度見直してみても、その形は変わらない。

　光は<ruby>悪意を笑い<rt>・・・・・</rt></ruby>、
　養母は声もなくそれを受けている。

　こんな事はかつてなかった。

　病に臥せる前、思春期ゆえのものだろう、光はしば
しば母親に対して反抗的な態度をとることもあった。
　が――このような目付きをしたためしはない。

　……目覚めたばかりで、なにか混乱でもあるのでは
ないか。
　そうとでも思わねば、納得しようもなかった。
